# What sevenx_multisite is made of

This page is for developers and administrators who want to open the `sevenx_multisite` package and know what every
file is for. It answers: which files the site package holds, what its `package.xml` declares, which packages it pulls
in, and which parts of a finished installation come from somewhere else.

## Contents

1. [The files of the site package](#the-files-of-the-site-package)
2. [What package.xml declares](#what-packagexml-declares)
3. [The settings files](#the-settings-files)
4. [The required packages](#the-required-packages)
5. [What is not in the packages](#what-is-not-in-the-packages)
6. [Opening the package yourself](#opening-the-package-yourself)

## The files of the site package

The folder `packages/sevenx_multisite/` of [se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage)
holds twelve files, and the published `sevenx_multisite.ezpkg` of 6.0.15 holds the same ones:

```text
package.xml
documents/LICENCE
files/default/image/logo.png
files/default/thumbnail/thumbnail.png
settings/ini-admin.php
settings/ini-common.php
settings/ini-site.php
settings/install-scripts.php
settings/post-install-fix.php
settings/preferences.php
settings/roles.php
settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php
```

There is no content and no class definition in the site package itself: those come from the packages it requires.

## What package.xml declares

| Element | Value in `sevenx_multisite` |
|---|---|
| `<package version>` | `6.0.15-0`, with `install_type="import"` |
| `<name>` | `sevenx_multisite` |
| `<summary>` | MultiSite Default Installation |
| `<vendor>` | `7x` |
| `<type value>` | `site` |
| `<ezpublish><version>` | `6.0.15-stable` (named version `6.0`) |
| `<version>` | number `6.0`, release `15-stable` |
| `<licence>` | `GPL`, with the text in `documents/LICENCE` |
| `<state>` | `stable` |
| `<maintainers>` | one maintainer with the role `lead` and a maintainer e-mail |
| `<files>` | a `default` collection with a `thumbnail` (`thumbnail.png`) and an `image` (`logo.png`), each with an `md5sum` |
| `<requires>` | `sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent`, both `type="ezpackage"`, `min-version="5.1"` |
| `<settings>` | seven `<settings-file>` entries, listed below |
| `<install>`, `<uninstall>` | empty: the package installs no items of its own |

The `<host>` in `<packaging>` names the machine the package was built on. The element-by-element reference is
[package.xml reference](../basics/package-xml-reference.md).

## The settings files

`CreateSites` (`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php`) includes every `<settings-file>` of the chosen site
package from its `settings/` folder, then calls the functions those files define when they exist. The seven files
listed in `sevenx_multisite`'s `package.xml`, in their order there:

| File | Defines | Calls on `sevenxMultiSiteInstaller` |
|---|---|---|
| `ini-site.php` | `eZSiteINISettings()` | `siteINISettings()`: settings of the public siteaccess |
| `ini-admin.php` | `eZSiteAdminINISettings()` | `adminINISettings()`: settings of the admin siteaccess |
| `ini-common.php` | `eZSiteCommonINISettings()` | `commonINISettings()`: settings written to `settings/override/` |
| `sevenx-multi-site-installer.php` | the class `sevenxMultiSiteInstaller` | (the class itself, 7692 lines) |
| `install-scripts.php` | `eZSitePreInstall()`, `eZSitePostInstall()` | `preInstall()` and `postInstall()` |
| `roles.php` | `eZSiteRoles()` | `siteRoles()` |
| `preferences.php` | `eZSitePreferences()` | `sitePreferences()` |

Each wrapper is a few lines: it creates a new `sevenxMultiSiteInstaller` with the parameters it was given and returns
what the method returns.

`post-install-fix.php` is the eighth file. It is **not** a `<settings-file>`: the installer loads it itself with
`require_once dirname( __FILE__ ) . '/post-install-fix.php';` on its first line of code. It holds the functions that
repair node placement, layout references, menus, tags and URL aliases after the content is in. See
[Post-install fixes](post-install-fixes.md).

> **Note**
> `sevenx_multisite` and `sevenx_multisite_clean` carry byte-identical copies of all eight PHP files. Only their
> `package.xml` differs: name, summary, description and the demo content package they require.

## The required packages

| Package | Type | Contents | Page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sevenx_classes` | `contentclass` | 33 class definitions in `ezcontentclass/`, `install_type="install"` | [sevenx_classes](sevenx-classes.md) |
| `sevenx_multisite_democontent` | `contentobject` | 31 class definitions, 291 object files, 194 image and file blobs in `simplefiles/` | [The demo content packages](the-demo-content-packages.md) |

How the setup resolves `<requires>` and in which order it installs them is described in
[Dependencies and install order](../basics/dependencies-and-install-order.md).

## What is not in the packages

Several parts of a finished installation do not travel in any `.ezpkg`:

| Part | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| The templates and design of both sites | the `sevenx_themes_media` extension (design `media`), with `sevenx_themes_simple` after it |
| The siteaccess settings of `bold` and `bold_ger` | shipped by `sevenx_themes_media` in `settings/siteaccess/bold` and `bold_ger`, completed by the installer |
| Layouts, zones, blocks, collections and rules | `extension/sevenx_themes_media/share/db_data.dba`, see [Layouts data and the share .dba files](layouts-data-and-share-dba.md) |
| Tags (`eztags`) and the star rating of the test product | the same `db_data.dba` |
| The newsletter classes and tree | the `cjw_newsletter` extension's own packages, imported by a post-install step |
| The admin layouts | `extension/explayouts/share/fragments/admin_layouts_db_data.dba` |

So the extensions must be in the installation before the site package is installed. The installer checks for some
of them (`exp_adminui`, `expai`, `sevenx_authentication_2fa`, `cjw_newsletter`) and skips their parts when they are
missing; the others are simply listed in `ActiveExtensions`.

## Opening the package yourself

An `.ezpkg` is a gzip-compressed tar archive, so the usual tools read it:

```bash
curl -sO https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
tar -tzf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
tar -xzOf sevenx_multisite.ezpkg package.xml | less
```

An imported copy lives under `var/storage/packages/7x/sevenx_multisite/` of any installation that installed it,
next to a `.cache` folder the kernel writes. More on the format: [The .ezpkg file](../basics/the-ezpkg-file.md).
